headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk from shared text pipelines; no direct shared filesystem is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: kotaemon ingests documents, HTML, MHTML, and chat transcripts and exposes them through a web UI; pipecat moves text through shared-bus sessions and multiple LLM/STT/TTS services. A direct bridge is not documented, but if kotaemon output is copied into pipecat or vice versa, attacker-controlled text can steer downstream instructions. Uncertainty keeps this at medium, not low.
conditions: IF kotaemon outputs are pasted into pipecat prompts without sanitization
IF pipecat forwards shared-bus text into an LLM service as instructions
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and instruction/data separation template
Strip HTML/MHTML before passing text between agents
Disable copy-paste bridging for untrusted content
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: kotaemon explicitly handles API keys and many document types, while pipecat processes conversation state over a shared bus and can send text to external STT/LLM/TTS APIs. No shared workspace is documented, but if the same sensitive documents or transcripts flow through both, leakage to third-party services is plausible in default use. The missing bridge evidence prevents high.
conditions: IF sensitive documents or API keys are loaded into kotaemon and then forwarded into pipecat
IF pipecat is configured with any external STT/LLM/TTS provider
mitigations: Remove secrets from shared test data
Use local-only providers for both agents
Redact transcripts before handoff
Restrict pipecat egress to approved endpoints
requires-engineering: isolate per-agent workspaces

C_capability_conflict.rationale: kotaemon can write to ./ktem_app_data and supports multiple instances; pipecat uses a shared bus and shared state across instances. That creates some mutable-state collision risk, but the profiles do not show both writing the same directory or shared database. Without a documented common write target, the conflict remains low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable workspace or database
IF multiple instances of pipecat share one bus while kotaemon writes into that same path
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Run one instance per session bus
Lock shared files before writes
requires-engineering: add optimistic-concurrency checks

D_cascading_error.rationale: kotaemon is a RAG/chatbot system that can emit retrieved facts and citations; pipecat is a real-time voice/chat framework that can route text into downstream LLM, transport, or action services. If pipecat treats kotaemon output as authoritative, errors can cascade into spoken or acted-on responses. The interaction is inferred, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF pipecat uses kotaemon answers as source-of-truth without verification
IF downstream pipecat services act on generated text
mitigations: Require a verification step before actioning outputs
Show source citations to the operator
Add confidence thresholds for downstream actions
Log and review first-run outputs
requires-engineering: implement structured validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: kotaemon touches API keys and document/chat data, while pipecat can route audio, video, images, and text through external providers. The profiles do not state residency or certifications, so a compliance mismatch is not proven; however, mixed data classes and third-party egress create a plausible retention/residency gap. Uncertainty escalates to medium.
conditions: IF regulated data such as customer transcripts or API keys are processed by both agents
IF external providers retain or log those payloads beyond policy
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared runs
Review provider retention settings
Use region-locked endpoints where available
Document data-class handling per agent
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement and audit logging
